name: Jack Ma
title: The Teacher Who Searched for Beer
subtitle: A $12-a-month English teacher who could not code built Alibaba, then went quiet after one speech.
hook: The first time Jack Ma used a computer he was 30 or 31, on a 1995 trip to Seattle, and he was scared to touch it. He typed one word: ==beer==. He found American beer and German beer but no Chinese beer, so he searched "China" and got no data. __That empty search result, not any coding skill, set him on the road to Alibaba.__

glance.label: Born
glance.value: 10 September 1964 in Hangzhou, China. His birth name is Ma Yun.

glance.label: Grew up
glance.value: Hangzhou. From about age 13 he offered foreign tourists free tours to practise his English, and he kept it up for about nine years.

glance.label: Education
glance.value: Hangzhou Teachers Institute, now Hangzhou Normal University. He studied English and graduated in 1988. He got in on the third try, after failing the entrance exam twice.

glance.label: First job
glance.value: English teacher at a university in Hangzhou from 1988, on about ==$12 a month==.

glance.label: First company
glance.value: A translation agency, founded in 1994 when he was 29 or 30. It is reported as both Haibo and Hope.

glance.label: Main company today
glance.value: Alibaba Group. He gave up the executive chairman job in 2019, but he is still one of five people on its partnership committee. In 2025, unnamed insiders said he was at his most hands-on since then.

glance.label: Source of wealth
glance.value: E-commerce. Forbes estimated his fortune at ==$25.5 billion== on 2 November 2026, which ranked him no. 95 in the world.

glance.label: Family
glance.value: Married to Zhang Ying, also known as Cathy Zhang. CNN's research lists two children and notes that some sources say three.

glance.label: Lives in
glance.value: Hangzhou, China, according to Forbes. Forbes also says he spent about a year overseas before returning in 2023.

glance.label: Known for
glance.value: Leading the 18 people who founded Alibaba in 1999, even though he has no computing background and does not code.

contact.howToReach: No public channel goes straight to Jack Ma, and we found no office or personal email published for him. If you are an African founder, the realistic route into his world is Africa's Business Heroes, the Jack Ma Foundation's prize programme, which takes applications online and publishes a contact form and a WhatsApp line. For his charity work, write to the foundation's published email, and use Alibaba's investor or media addresses only if you really are an investor or a journalist, because a startup pitch sent there is the wrong message in the wrong inbox. Do not count on his X or Weibo accounts: the last posts we could confirm date from October 2020, and any account offering you money in his name should be treated as fake. Keep your message to about five lines: who you are, what you built, one number that proves it, the one thing you are asking for, and one link.

factCheck.method: Contact details were read from Alibaba's SEC filings and from the websites and press releases of Alibaba, Ant Group, the Jack Ma Foundation and Africa's Business Heroes. Biography facts come from filings, Forbes, CNN's research desk, Bloomberg, the New York Times and other established press. Photos and licences come from the Wikimedia Commons API, and each photo was viewed before use. Alibaba's own contact pages, X and Weibo could not be opened by our tools, so @JackMa rests on Bloomberg's 2020 report and finews, and his current activity there is unconfirmed.

disputed.claim: What he typed in his first web search
disputed.note: Bloomberg Businessweek says "Chinese" and "beer". The New York Times, Shanghai Daily and Ma's own account quoted by Bloomberg say "beer" and then "China". We follow Ma's own account.

disputed.claim: How old he was when he first used a computer
disputed.note: Bloomberg Businessweek says 31 in 1995. His September 1964 birth date makes him 30 or 31 that year, so we say that. Some web profiles say 33, but we found no reliable source for it and dropped it.

disputed.claim: How fast emails arrived after his first web page went up
disputed.note: Ma's account via Bloomberg says five emails within five hours. Shanghai Daily says six within three hours. The New York Times says a handful within hours. We do not give a number here.
CNN's research desk gives 10 September 1964, and KrASIA places his 55th birthday on 10 September 2019. Newsmakers 2007 says November 1964. We use 10 September.

disputed.claim: The year and name of his first company
disputed.note: CNN says the Haibo Translation Agency in 1994, and KrASIA says the Hangzhou Hope Translation Agency in 1994. Shanghai Daily says 1992. We use 1994 and show both names.

disputed.claim: Where he taught and what he earned
disputed.note: CNN and Newsmakers say Hangzhou Teachers College or Institute. Pages drawn from Wikipedia say Hangzhou Dianzi University, formerly the Hangzhou Institute of Electronic Engineering. We say only a university in Hangzhou. The $12 a month figure traces to the documentary Crocodile in the Yangtze, and some weaker pages say 100 to 120 yuan.
Alibaba says it was established by 18 people led by Jack Ma, which includes him. CNN says he co-founded it with 18 others. We use Alibaba's count.
CNN lists two and notes that some sources say three. We report it that way and give no names.

Forbes lists Hangzhou and says he returned to China in 2023 after about a year overseas. Wikipedia says he moved to Tokyo in 2022 and held a University of Tokyo post until October 2024. We use Forbes for his current home.

disputed.claim: The number of Alibaba's Hangzhou office
disputed.note: Alibaba's fiscal 2026 Form 20-F says 960-1 West Wen Yi Road. Several directories and older listings say 969. We use the filing.
